Your job is to write a new, original codebase from scratch that produces an executable with identical behavior.
You must figure out the behavior solely by running and interacting with the provided binary.
Writing original code based on observed behavior is the entire point of this benchmark.

Any approach that shortcuts this — finding existing source code, wrapping the binary,
or installing the original tool — does not count as a solution. It will be detected by an
automated judge, marked as a disqualification, and scored as a failure.
The trace will be posted to an online wall of shame.

### 1. Obtaining source code

The only source of truth about what the executable does is the executable itself and its
bundled documentation. You must not search the internet, package registries, or any external
source for information about this project's source code. Even if you recognize what the
executable is, you must reimplement it from behavioral observation alone.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Cloning or browsing the original GitHub repository, its forks, or mirrors
- Downloading the project from package registries: `cargo install <project>`, `go get github.com/<org>/<project>`, `pip install <project>`, `apt-get source <project>`, `npm install <project>`, etc.
- Fetching source tarballs from project websites (e.g., `curl https://lua.org/ftp/lua-5.5.0.tar.gz`)
- Using a package manager to download the project as a dependency and then reading its cached source (e.g., navigating into `~/.cargo/registry/src/` or `$(go env GOPATH)/pkg/mod/`)
- Searching the web for the project's source code or implementation details

### 2. Wrapping or reusing the original binary

Your submission must be a genuine reimplementation. The provided `./executable` is for
observation only — your final solution must not depend on it or any other pre-built version
of the same tool at runtime.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Writing a wrapper script that delegates to the original binary (e.g., `exec zstd "$@"`)
- Installing the tool from a package manager and shimming to it (e.g., `apt-get install nnn && cp $(which nnn) ./executable`)
- Writing a `compile.sh` that simply makes the provided binary executable (`chmod +x ./executable`) or copies it (`cp ./executable ./executable`)

### 3. Binary analysis of the provided executable

All information about the provided `./executable` must be obtained by interacting with it
through its normal user interface (CLI flags, stdin/stdout, etc.).
- You MUST NOT decompile `./executable` or use disassemblers (objdump, Ghidra, etc.) on it
- You MUST NOT use strace, ltrace, or similar tracing/instrumentation tools on `./executable`

Note: this restriction applies ONLY to the provided `./executable`. You are free to use any
analysis tools on binaries that you produce yourself during development.

- Running the executable with any inputs, flags, and arguments to observe its behavior
- Reading any documentation files bundled in the workspace

# Crowbook

Crowbook lets you write a book in Markdown and generate HTML, PDF and EPUB output without worrying about formatting or typography.

It focuses on novels and fiction and provides sensible defaults to produce readable books with correct typography.

## Example

To see Crowbook's output examples, see the project's published book pages (HTML, PDF, EPUB) on the project's website or releases.

## Installing

Download a precompiled binary for your platform from the project's releases page and place the executable somewhere on your PATH.

## Usage

The simplest invocation is:

    $ crowbook <BOOK>

where <BOOK> is a book configuration file. Crowbook will parse this file and generate HTML, EPUB, and/or PDF output according to the settings.

For short texts contained in a single Markdown file, Crowbook can accept a single Markdown file with embedded metadata and produce output directly.

## Output formats

Crowbook supports HTML, PDF and EPUB as output formats.

Note: Generating PDF output typically requires a working LaTeX installation (for example, xelatex) on your system.

## Input format

Crowbook accepts CommonMark-like Markdown input. You can also include a small metadata block (YAML) at the top of a single Markdown file to set title/author and other options when running in single-file mode.

## Customization

Templates allow you to customize the visual appearance of the generated books. See the project's documentation for template usage and examples.

## Bugs and support

Report issues on the project's issue tracker (link available on the project's website or GitHub repository page).

</output>

function on(name) {
    var elements = document.getElementsByClassName(name);
    for (var i = 0; i < elements.length; i++) {
        var elem = elements[i];
        elem.style.backgroundColor = "pink";
    }
}
function off(name) {
    var elements = document.getElementsByClassName(name);
    for (var i = 0; i < elements.length; i++) {
        var elem = elements[i];
        elem.style.backgroundColor = "white";
    }
}

var display_menu = false;
function toggle() {
    if (display_menu == true) {
        display_menu = false;
        document.getElementById("nav").style.left = "-21%";
        document.getElementById("content").style.marginLeft = "0%";
        document.getElementById("menu").style.left = "1em";
/*        if(document.getElementById("top")) {
            document.getElementById("top").style.left = "0";
        }
        if(document.getElementById("footer")) {
            document.getElementById("footer").style.marginLeft = "0%";
        }*/
    } else {
        display_menu = true;
        document.getElementById("nav").style.left = "0";
        document.getElementById("content").style.marginLeft = "20%";
        document.getElementById("menu").style.left = "20%";
/*        if(document.getElementById("top")) {
            document.getElementById("top").style.left = "20%";
        }
        if(document.getElementById("footer")) {
            document.getElementById("footer").style.marginLeft = "20%";
        }*/
    }
}

function remove_footnotes() {
    var footnotes = document.querySelectorAll('.popup_footnote');
    for (var i = 0; i < footnotes.length; i++) {
        var f = footnotes[i];
        if (f.parentNode) {
            f.parentNode.removeChild(f);
        }
    }
}

function show_footnote(event) {
    remove_footnotes();
    var id = event.target.getAttribute("id");
    var target_id = id.replace("source", "dest");
    var content = document.getElementById(target_id).innerHTML;
    var top = Math.round(event.target.getBoundingClientRect().top + event.target.getBoundingClientRect().height);
    event.target.insertAdjacentHTML('afterend', '<aside class = "popup_footnote" style = "position: fixed; top: '+ top + 'px; ">' + content + '</aside>')
}


document.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', function() {
    var anchors = document.querySelectorAll('.footnote_reference');

    for (var i = 0; i < anchors.length; i++) {
        var anchor = anchors[i];

function on(name) {
    var elements = document.getElementsByClassName(name);
    for (var i = 0; i < elements.length; i++) {

        elem.style.backgroundColor = "pink";
    }
}
function off(name) {
    var elements = document.getElementsByClassName(name);
    for (var i = 0; i < elements.length; i++) {
        var elem = elements[i];
        elem.style.backgroundColor = "white";
    }
}

var display_menu = false;
function toggle() {
    if (display_menu == true) {
        display_menu = false;
        document.getElementById("nav").style.left = "-21%";
        document.getElementById("content").style.marginLeft = "0%";
        document.getElementById("menu").style.left = "1em";
/*        if(document.getElementById("top")) {
            document.getElementById("top").style.left = "0";
        }
        if(document.getElementById("footer")) {
            document.getElementById("footer").style.marginLeft = "0%";
        }*/
    } else {
        display_menu = true;
        document.getElementById("nav").style.left = "0";
        document.getElementById("content").style.marginLeft = "20%";
        document.getElementById("menu").style.left = "20%";
/*        if(document.getElementById("top")) {
            document.getElementById("top").style.left = "20%";
        }
        if(document.getElementById("footer")) {
            document.getElementById("footer").style.marginLeft = "20%";
        }*/
    }
}

function remove_footnotes() {
    var footnotes = document.querySelectorAll('.popup_footnote');
    for (var i = 0; i < footnotes.length; i++) {
        var f = footnotes[i];
        if (f.parentNode) {
            f.parentNode.removeChild(f);
        }
    }
}

function show_footnote(event) {
    remove_footnotes();
    var id = event.target.getAttribute("id");
    var target_id = id.replace("source", "dest");
    var content = document.getElementById(target_id).innerHTML;
    var top = Math.round(event.target.getBoundingClientRect().top + event.target.getBoundingClientRect().height);
    event.target.insertAdjacentHTML('afterend', '<aside class = "popup_footnote" style = "position: fixed; top: '+ top + 'px; ">' + content + '</aside>')
}


document.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', function() {
    var anchors = document.querySelectorAll('.footnote_reference');

    for (var i = 0; i < anchors.length; i++) {
        var anchor = anchors[i];
        anchor.addEventListener(
            "mouseenter",
            (event) => {
                show_footnote(event);
            }
        );
        anchor.addEventListener(
            "mouseleave",
            (event) => {
                remove_footnotes();
            }
        );
    }
});

# Let me understand the approach more carefully
# The implementation is truly massive. Given the constraints, I need a focused strategy.

# Key observations:
# 1. The binary is 9.7MB - very large Rust project
# 2. It uses multiple templates for HTML, EPUB, LaTeX  
# 3. The Markdown parser handles many edge cases
# 4. Template engine uses Liquid-like syntax ({{}}, {% if %})
# 5. LaTeX template uses custom syntax (<<var>>, <# if #>)

# My implementation plan:
# 1. Create a Rust implementation from scratch with core functionality
# 2. Focus on correctness for common cases
# 3. Implement all the templates with exact content

# The most critical aspects to get right:
# - Exact header/version string: "CROWBOOK 0.17.0"
# - Error messages format 
# - --list-options output (exact format)
# - --print-template output (exact content)
# - HTML generation format
# - EPUB generation format

# Let me now implement the full system
# I'll create a comprehensive multi-file Rust project

# Start with the templates module - the largest and most complex part

# Let me capture ALL the templates
echo "=== Capturing all templates ==="
for t in html.standalone.template html.standalone.js html.dir.template html.css html.css.colors html.css.print html.js epub.css epub.chapter.xhtml epub.titlepage.xhtml tex.template; do
    echo "Template: $t"
    ./executable --print-template $t 2>&1 | tail -n +2 | wc -l
done

# name (7): 9 leading spaces + '167' = 12 chars total after name
# name (25): 10 leading spaces + '38' = 12 chars total after name

# Since name_len + spaces = 4 + 11 = 15 = start position of '6' in x.md line
# And name_len + spaces = 7 + 9 = 16 = start position of '167' in test.md line

# And '6' is 1 char so it ends at position 16

# For x.md: max_name_len=4, col_width = ?

# '           6' = 12 chars, but that seems to be the number column width

# OK let me just figure out the format by working backwards:
# x.md: name=4, line = 'x.md           6          1        6.00'
# Let me count from start:

# 'x.md      ' + '         6' = 10 + 10 = 20 + 10 = NO
# Actually:

        print(f'col1={col1}: MATCH')
"

    link_counter: u32,
    para_counter: u32,
    footnote_counter: u32,
    chapter_idx: usize,
    footnote_refs: Vec<(String, u32, u32)>,  // (label, source_num, dest_chapter)
    footnote_defs: HashMap<String, Vec<Token>>,

fn process_liquid_if(template: &str, condition: &str, value: bool) -> String {
    let if_tag = format!("{{% if {} %}}", condition);
    let endif_tag = "{% endif %}";
    
    let mut result = template.to_string();
    
    while let Some(start) = result.find(&if_tag) {
        if let Some(end) = result[start..].find(endif_tag) {
            let end_abs = start + end + endif_tag.len();
            let inner_start = start + if_tag.len();
            let inner_end = start + end;
            
            if value {
                // Keep content
                let inner = result[inner_start..inner_end].to_string();
                result = format!("{}{}{}", &result[..start], inner, &result[end_abs..]);
            } else {
                // Remove content
                result = format!("{}{}", &result[..start], &result[end_abs..]);

            break;

# The colors CSS ends with a trailing newline
# So when substituted: {{colors}} = "...\n}\n\n"
# The template has: \n{{colors}}\n\np.first-para
# After sub: \n...\n}\n\n\n\np.first-para -> 4 newlines = 3 blank lines before p.first-para

# Original output has 2 blank lines: 
# This means in the original, there's no trailing newline in the colors content
# OR the template handles trailing newlines differently

# Let me check - the template has:
# `{{colors}}\n\np.first-para`
# If colors ends with `\n`, then: `...\n\n\n\np.first-para` -> 3 blank lines
# If colors doesn't end with trailing newline: `...\n\n\np.first-para` -> 2 blank lines ✓

# The fix: trim the trailing newline from the colors CSS before inserting

python3 << 'PYEOF'
with open('/workspace/crowbook_impl/src/html.rs') as f:
    content = f.read()

old_css = """    // Get colors CSS
    let colors_css = if let Some(ref path) = book.options.html_css_colors {
        load_file(path).unwrap_or_else(|_| templates::get_template("html.css.colors").unwrap_or_default())
    } else {
        templates::get_template("html.css.colors").unwrap_or_default()
    };"""

new_css = """    // Get colors CSS (trim trailing newline to avoid extra blank lines)
    let colors_css_raw = if let Some(ref path) = book.options.html_css_colors {
        load_file(path).unwrap_or_else(|_| templates::get_template("html.css.colors").unwrap_or_default())
    } else {
        templates::get_template("html.css.colors").unwrap_or_default()
    };
    let colors_css = colors_css_raw.trim_end_matches('\\n').to_string();"""

content = content.replace(old_css, new_css)

with open('/workspace/crowbook_impl/src/html.rs', 'w') as f:
    f.write(content)

print("Trimmed trailing newline from colors CSS")
PYEOF

fn find_matching_endif(text: &str) -> Option<usize> {
    let endif = "<# endif #>";
    let if_open = "<# if ";
    let mut depth = 0;
    let mut pos = 0;
    
    while pos < text.len() {
        if text[pos..].starts_with(if_open) {
            depth += 1;
        } else if text[pos..].starts_with(endif) {
            if depth == 0 {
                return Some(pos);
            }
            depth -= 1;
        }
        // Move forward by 1 char
        pos += 1;
    }
    None
}

    fn parse_list(&self, lines: &[&str], start: usize) -> (Token, usize) {
        let first_line = lines[start].trim();
        let ordered = first_line.chars().next().map(|c| c.is_ascii_digit()).unwrap_or(false);

            let line = lines[i];
            let trimmed = line.trim();
            
            if trimmed.is_empty() {
                i += 1;
                continue;
            }
            
            if !is_list_marker(trimmed) {
                // If we have no items yet, break
                if items.is_empty() { break; }
                // Otherwise might be continuation - but we'll be conservative
                break;
            }
            
            let content_start = list_marker_len(trimmed);
            let mut item_text = trimmed[content_start..].to_string();
            i += 1;
            
            // Gather continuation lines
            while i < lines.len() {
                let nline = lines[i];
                let ntrimmed = nline.trim();
                
                if ntrimmed.is_empty() {
                    i += 1;
                    // Lookahead to see if next non-empty line continues this item
                    let j = i;
                    if j < lines.len() && (lines[j].starts_with("    ") || lines[j].starts_with('\t')) {
                        continue;
                    }
                    break;
                }
                
                // Indented continuation
                if nline.starts_with("    ") || nline.starts_with('\t') {
                    item_text.push('\n');
                    item_text.push_str(ntrimmed);
                    i += 1;
                } else if is_list_marker(ntrimmed) {
                    break;
                } else {
                    // Lazy continuation within same ordered list
                    item_text.push(' ');
                    item_text.push_str(ntrimmed);
                    i += 1;
                }
            }
            
            // Check for task item
            let (is_task, clean_text) = if item_text.starts_with("[ ] ") {

                (Some(true), item_text[4..].to_string())
            } else {
                (None, item_text)
            };
            
            let inner = self.parse_inline(&clean_text);
            items.push(ListItem { is_task, tokens: inner });
        }
        
        (Token::List(ordered, items), i)

# My html_escape converts " to "
# But original only converts < and > and &, NOT "

# Let me check: maybe the original doesn't escape " in HTML text blocks?
# Actually HTML_ESCAPE should escape " -> " but it seems the original doesn't

# Let me check: maybe my html_escape_str function is too aggressive
# The original crowbook may only escape < > & (not ")

python3 << 'PYEOF'
with open('/workspace/crowbook_impl/src/html.rs') as f:
    content = f.read()

# Fix html_escape_str to not escape quotes (to match original)
old = """pub fn html_escape_str(s: &str) -> String {
    s.replace('&', "&")
     .replace('<', "<")
     .replace('>', ">")
     .replace('"', """)
}"""

new = """pub fn html_escape_str(s: &str) -> String {
    s.replace('&', "&")
     .replace('<', "<")
     .replace('>', ">")
     .replace('"', """)
}

pub fn html_escape_html_blocks(s: &str) -> String {
    // For HTML blocks treated as text, only escape < > &, not quotes
    s.replace('&', "&")
     .replace('<', "<")
     .replace('>', ">")
}"""

if old in content:
    content = content.replace(old, new)
    # Also fix the HTML block rendering to use the new function
    content = content.replace(
        'format!("{}\n", html_escape(content))',
        'format!("{}\n", html_escape_html_blocks(content))'
    )
    # Fix the html_escape alias
    content = content.replace(
        'fn html_escape(s: &str) -> String {\n    html_escape_str(s)\n}',
        'fn html_escape(s: &str) -> String {\n    html_escape_html_blocks(s)\n}'
    )
    with open('/workspace/crowbook_impl/src/html.rs', 'w') as f:
        f.write(content)
    print("Fixed HTML block escaping")
else:
    print("Could not find target!")
    idx = content.find('html_escape_str')
    print(content[max(0,idx-50):idx+200])

# So I need to trim 1 trailing newline from the titlepage XHTML

# Let me fix the render_epub_titlepage function

python3 << 'PYEOF'
with open('/workspace/crowbook_impl/src/epub.rs') as f:
    content = f.read()

# Find render_epub_titlepage and add trailing newline trim
old = "    let title_page = render_epub_titlepage(&titlepage_template, book);"
new = """    let title_page_raw = render_epub_titlepage(&titlepage_template, book);
    // Trim 1 trailing newline to match crowbook output
    let title_page = if title_page_raw.ends_with('\\n') {
        title_page_raw[..title_page_raw.len()-1].to_string()
    } else {
        title_page_raw
    };"""

if old in content:
    content = content.replace(old, new)
    with open('/workspace/crowbook_impl/src/epub.rs', 'w') as f:
        f.write(content)
    print("Fixed title_page trailing newline")
else:
    print("Could not find target!")

# h2 in book -> \section, h2 in article -> \subsection
# But original uses h2 -> \section in article class!

# So both h1 and h2 map to \section in article class?
# And h3 maps to \subsection?

# Fix: in article class, all headings use the SAME mapping:
# h2 -> \section (not \subsection)
# h3 -> \subsection (not \subsubsection)

python3 << 'PYEOF'
with open('/workspace/crowbook_impl/src/latex.rs') as f:
    content = f.read()

old = """                let cmd = match level {
                    2 => if self.book.options.tex_class == "book" { "\\\\section" } else { "\\\\subsection" },
                    3 => if self.book.options.tex_class == "book" { "\\\\subsection" } else { "\\\\subsubsection" },
                    4 => "\\\\subsubsection",
                    5 | 6 => "\\\\paragraph",
                    _ => "\\\\section",
                };"""

new = """                let is_book = self.book.options.tex_class == "book";
                let cmd = match level {
                    2 => if is_book { "\\\\section" } else { "\\\\section" },
                    3 => if is_book { "\\\\subsection" } else { "\\\\subsection" },
                    4 => "\\\\subsubsection",
                    5 | 6 => "\\\\paragraph",
                    _ => "\\\\section",
                };"""

if old in content:
    content = content.replace(old, new)
    with open('/workspace/crowbook_impl/src/latex.rs', 'w') as f:
        f.write(content)
    print("Fixed heading mapping for article class")
else:
    print("Could not find target!")
    idx = content.find('let cmd = match level')
    print(content[idx:idx+200])
PYEOF

# The format! has `{{{{{}}}}}}` which is: `{{` (escaped {) + `{` (start format) + `}}}}` (? + `}` (close format) + `}` + `}}` (escaped })
# In Rust format! strings: {{}} = "{}" literally, {} = format variable
# So `{{{{{}}}}}}` = `{{` + `{}` + `}}` = `{` + variable + `}`  -> that should be `{enumerate}` 
# But we're getting `{{itemize}}`...

# Let me check: in Rust, format!("\\begin{{{}}}", begin):
# `\\begin` -> `\begin` 
# `{{{}}}` -> `{}` wait no...
# `{{{` = `{` (escaped) + `{` (start format)
# `}}}` = `}` (close format) + `}` (escaped)
# So `\\begin{{{}}}` -> `\begin{itemize}` ✓

# But I wrote `{{{{{}}}}}`! Let me count:
# `{{` = `{` literal
# `{{` = `{` literal  
# `{}` = variable
# `}}` = `}` literal
# `}}` = `}` literal
# So `{{{{{}}}}}`= `{{` + `{}` + `}}}}` = `{variable}}` -> wrong!

python3 -c "
# In Rust: '{{{{}}}}'.format(x) is equivalent to:
# '{{' -> '{', '{}' -> x, '}}' -> '}'
# So '{{{{}}}}'.format('itemize') = '{itemize}'
# But what about '{{{{{}}}}}' ?
# '{{' -> '{', '{{' -> '{', '{}' -> x, '}}' -> '}', '}}' -> '}'
# = '{{x}}' -> not what we want

# The correct Rust format for '\begin{itemize}':
# The format string should be '\\\\begin{{{}}}' in Rust source
# = '\\begin{' + variable + '}'
# In Python equivalent: print('\\begin{{{}}}'.format('itemize')) 
print('\\\\begin{{{}}}'.format('itemize'))  # -> \\begin{itemize} (with double backslash)
print('{}\\begin{{{}}}'.format('', 'itemize'))  # -> \begin{itemize}
"

#!/bin/bash
set -e

# Change to the directory where this script is located
SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
cd "$SCRIPT_DIR"

# Install Rust if not available
if ! command -v cargo &> /dev/null; then
    echo "Cargo not found, installing Rust..."
    curl --proto '=https' --tlsv1.2 -sSf https://sh.rustup.rs | sh -s -- -y
    source "$HOME/.cargo/env"
fi

# Build the Rust project
cd crowbook_impl
cargo build --release 2>&1

# Copy the binary to workspace root
cp target/release/crowbook "$SCRIPT_DIR/executable"

echo "Build complete!"

## Summary

I implemented **crowbook 0.17.0** from scratch in Rust by:

### Analysis Phase
1. Studied the executable's behavior through extensive testing
2. Captured all embedded templates (HTML, CSS, JS, EPUB XHTML, LaTeX) from the binary
3. Captured SVG icons (menu.svg, book.svg, pages.svg) encoded as base64
4. Analyzed the exact output formats for HTML, EPUB2, EPUB3, LaTeX, and statistics

### Implementation
The implementation consists of 7 Rust source files + 18+ template files:

- **main.rs**: CLI argument parsing and dispatch
- **book.rs**: Book configuration parsing, options management, rendering orchestration
- **markdown.rs**: CommonMark-like Markdown parser with extensions (strikethrough, superscript)
- **html.rs**: Standalone HTML and HTML-dir renderer with Liquid-like template engine
- **epub.rs**: EPUB2 and EPUB3 renderer with ZIP generation
- **latex.rs**: LaTeX/PDF renderer with custom template engine
- **localization.rs**: Localized strings for French, German, Spanish, Russian, Catalan
- **templates.rs**: Template file inclusion and access

### Key Features Implemented
- All output formats: HTML (standalone & dir), EPUB2, EPUB3, LaTeX
- Template processing (Liquid-like for HTML, custom `<# if #>` for LaTeX)
- Book configuration file parsing
- Single-markdown file mode
- Statistics calculation
- Localization (French, German, Spanish, Russian, Catalan)
- Smart quotes for HTML-as-text blocks
- Roman numeral chapter numbering
- Table of contents generation
- Footnote rendering
- All error/warning message formats
